description: I'm an 11th-grade student from Türkiye interested in physics, space science, and technology. I enjoy research, problem-solving, and teamwork. I'm looking for creative, motivated teammates with skills in coding, engineering, data analysis, or design to develop innovative solutions together.
summary:
In the MINDSPACE project, we wanted to solve a major problem: astronauts on long space missions face massive physical and psychological wear and tear from radiation, isolation, and altered gravity. With communication delays back to Earth, they really need a way to catch health issues early and handle them on their own.
That is why we designed MINDSPACE a compact, smart companion robot for the space station. Thanks to advanced subdermal chips under the astronaut's skin, it continuously tracks everything from heart rate and fatigue to blood sugar, blood oxygen, and bone health. Inside the robot, an ESP32 chip compares these numbers against a 7-day personal baseline. If something is off like high stress or bad sleep he robot steps in with voice prompts, a matte OLED screen, or LED alerts, and even explains its reasoning with a "Why am I seeing this?" feature. When an astronaut is stressed or tired, it can even play their favorite music to help them mentally unwind, taking care of both their body and mind.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

MINDSPACE is an all-in-one smart health companion robot for astronauts on long missions. It tracks vital metrics—heart rate, fatigue, blood sugar, oxygen, and bone health—via advanced subdermal chips under the skin. An embedded ESP32 microcontroller processes this data locally, comparing it against a 7-day personal baseline to instantly spot health anomalies without Earth communication delays.

What benefits does it have?

It provides autonomous, non-invasive, and continuous physical and mental health monitoring, allowing astronauts to detect issues early before they become mission-threatening emergencies.

What is the intended impact of the project?

To safeguard astronaut health and psychological resilience during prolonged deep-space isolation by bridging automated tracking with proactive emotional support.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Python for local data scripting, an ESP32 microcontroller for edge processing, Tinkercad for 3D modeling, alongside matte OLED displays, LED indicators, and audio interfaces.

How is your project creative?

It uniquely combines physical health metrics (via subdermal chips) with psychological interventions into a friendly robot. It features an interactive persona, a "Why am I seeing this?" transparent explanation feature, and proactive musical therapy for stress relief.

What factors did your team consider?

Communication latency with Earth, the psychological toll of isolation, low-power edge computing (ESP32), and non-invasive continuous data collection that does not encumber astronauts.
